The main barrier in transferring semantic pixel-wise seg- mentation architectures to agriculture is limited availability of labelled datasets [12]. Therefore, an important contribu- tion of our work is training and performance evaluation of the segmentation network on a new image dataset collected speciﬁcally for the agricultural domain. The images were collected during tractor’s operation in the crop ﬁeld and represent a realistic scenario for driving in the agricultural environment. The dataset contains ﬁve labelled classes of ﬁeld structures: “Vegetation”, “Grass”, “Ground”, “Crop ﬁeld”, and “Obstacle”. Moreover, we present an approach for continuous quali- tative validation of the network in practice. The approach is based on a tool for real-time visualization of segmentation results for images captured by the vehicle’s camera during 2020 16th International Conference on Control, Automation, Robotics and Vision (ICARCV) December 13-15, 2020. Andersen 1 Abstract— The development of autonomous agricultural ve- hicles depends on accurate visual interpretation of the envi- ronment. Semantic pixel-wise segmentation plays an important role in achieving a more detailed description of the scene and understanding of the spatial-relationship between different objects. In this paper, a deep architecture for road scene and indoor scene segmentation, SegNet, is applied in solving the scene recognition problem for the agricultural environment. The network is trained on an agriculture image dataset collected during ﬁeld operation. The problem focuses on the segmentation of ﬁve classes of structures commonly found in the ﬁelds: vegetation, grass, ground, crop ﬁeld and obstacles. We apply frequency balancing to address the challenge of class imbalance and transfer learning technique.
